sources.entry: Yopass - Secure sharing of secrets, passwords and files. (Demo) Apache-2.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Yopass is a self-hosted service for sharing passwords, files, and other secrets through links that encrypt in the browser before anything reaches the server.
summary.what_it_does: The browser generates a random key and encrypts the secret with OpenPGP before upload, and the decryption key stays in the URL fragment, which is never sent to the server. The server stores only the encrypted message with an expiration time. Links can be one-time (removed after first retrieval) or remain valid until expiry, with optional custom durations and optional password protection. The standard flow needs no user accounts. Storage can be Redis or Memcached for messages and disk or S3-compatible storage for files. The project also includes a command-line client, split read/write deployments with read-only mode, Prometheus metrics, and translations. A business license adds OpenID Connect, theming, audit logging, secret requests, read receipts, signed webhooks, and file uploads larger than 1 MB.
use_cases: share passwords without email or chat
share encrypted files with a recipient
share credentials from the terminal via CLI
run read-only secret retrieval separate from creation
notable: Browser-side OpenPGP encryption; decryption key lives in the URL fragment and never reaches the server
No accounts or tracking for the standard flow
Disk and S3/MinIO file storage options
Kubernetes manifest and Docker Compose examples with Let's Encrypt
caveats: Production use requires HTTPS, so a TLS setup or reverse proxy must be configured
Several features (OIDC, audit logs, webhooks, read receipts, larger file uploads, theming) require a business license
The quick-start setup runs without TLS and is meant only for local testing or behind a TLS-terminating proxy
